subproblems.title: A scalar multiple of a boundary is supported in the support: S = c·∂T ⇒ spt S ⊆ spt T
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P (U : Set (Euclid P)), T ∈ 𝒟_{n+1}(U) and S ∈ 𝒟_n(U) (GeometricCurrentOn U (n+1), GeometricCurrentOn U n) and c ∈ ℝ. If S(ω) = c·∂T(ω) for every test n-form ω in U (∂T = T.boundary, ∂T(ω) = T(dω)), then spt S ⊆ spt T (GeometricCurrentOn.support, Simon 6.2.11).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U (n + 1)) (S : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (c : ℝ), (∀ ω : TestFormOn U n, S ω = c * T.boundary ω) → S.support ⊆ T.support
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Step 1 (a) and Step 7 of the parent proof ("if B vanishes on an open O with compact closure, so does ∂B ... and hence Z = c·∂B"; "spt X ⊆ spt Y: if O is open with compact closure and Y vanishes on O, then so does X = Y.boundary"), stated once for an arbitrary constant c.
Notation. For a current V ∈ 𝒟_j(U), its zero region Z(V) (GeometricCurrentOn.zeroRegion) is the union of all sets W such that W is open, closure W is compact, closure W ⊆ U, and V vanishes on W (V.VanishesOn W: V(η) = 0 for every test j-form η in U with tsupport η ⊆ W). By definition spt V = U ∖ Z(V) (GeometricCurrentOn.support).

1. Let W be one of the sets whose union is Z(T): W is open, closure W is compact, closure W ⊆ U, and T(η) = 0 for every test (n+1)-form η in U with tsupport η ⊆ W.
2. Let ω be a test n-form in U with tsupport ω ⊆ W. The test (n+1)-form dω := exteriorDerivativeTestOn U n ω has underlying form exteriorDerivative ω, and tsupport(dω) ⊆ tsupport ω ⊆ W by tsupport_exteriorDerivative_subset. Hence T(dω) = 0 by step 1.
3. By the hypothesis and GeometricCurrentOn.boundary_apply (∂T(ω) = T(dω)), S(ω) = c·∂T(ω) = c·T(dω) = c·0 = 0. Since ω was arbitrary, S vanishes on W; W has the required openness and compactness properties, so W is one of the sets whose union is Z(S), i.e. W ⊆ Z(S).
4. As W was an arbitrary member of the family defining Z(T), Z(T) ⊆ Z(S). Therefore spt S = U ∖ Z(S) ⊆ U ∖ Z(T) = spt T. ∎
proof_key_steps: Take W in the family defining the zero region of T (open, relatively compact in U, T vanishes on W).
For a test form ω with tsupport ω ⊆ W, tsupport dω ⊆ tsupport ω ⊆ W, so T(dω) = 0 and S(ω) = c·T(dω) = 0.
Hence W lies in the zero region of S; so zeroRegion T ⊆ zeroRegion S and spt S = U ∖ zeroRegion S ⊆ U ∖ zeroRegion T = spt T.

subproblems.title: For an integer multiplicity current on ℝ^P and closed F: spt T ⊆ F iff R.measure(Fᶜ) = 0
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, T ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) (GeometricCurrentOn univ n) and let R be an integer multiplicity representation (IMRep univ n) with R.Represents T. Let F ⊆ ℝ^P be closed. Then spt T ⊆ F if and only if R.measure(ℝ^P ∖ F) = 0, where R.measure = θ·H^n⌞M is the weight measure (μHE[n].restrict R.carrier).withDensity R.mult.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (T : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n) (R : IMRep (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n) (F : Set (Euclid P)), R.Represents T → IsClosed F → (T.support ⊆ F ↔ R.measure Fᶜ = 0)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Step 1 (b) of the parent proof (R_T.measure(ℝ^P ∖ spt T) = 0 via imrep_carrier_sdiff_support_null) and Step 6 of the parent proof ("If x ∉ F, choose ε > 0 with ball(x, ε) ⊆ ℝ^P ∖ F; then R_B.measure(ball(x, ε)) = 0, so x ∉ spt B by dimred_im_mass_measure (b)"), combined into one equivalence.
Accepted results cited by name (dependencies of ancestors of this node): imrep_carrier_sdiff_support_null (∀ P n U T R, IsOpen U → R.Represents T → μHE[n] (R.carrier \ T.support) = 0) and dimred_im_mass_measure (its part (b): ∀ x ∈ U, x ∈ T.support ↔ ∀ ε > 0, R.measure (ball x ε) ≠ 0, for IsOpen U and R.Represents T).
Write σ := R.measure = (μHE[n].restrict R.carrier).withDensity (x ↦ R.mult x).

1. (spt T)ᶜ is open. Since the domain is ℝ^P, spt T = ℝ^P ∖ Z(T), where Z(T) = T.zeroRegion; hence (spt T)ᶜ = Z(T), which is open (GeometricCurrentOn.isOpen_zeroRegion, a union of open sets). In particular (spt T)ᶜ is a Borel set.
2. σ((spt T)ᶜ) = 0. By imrep_carrier_sdiff_support_null, applied with U = ℝ^P (open) and R representing T, μHE[n](R.carrier ∖ spt T) = 0. Because (spt T)ᶜ is measurable, (μHE[n].restrict R.carrier)((spt T)ᶜ) = μHE[n]((spt T)ᶜ ∩ R.carrier) = μHE[n](R.carrier ∖ spt T) = 0. A measure with density is absolutely continuous with respect to its base measure (withDensity_absolutelyContinuous), so σ((spt T)ᶜ) = 0.
3. (⇒) Assume spt T ⊆ F. Then Fᶜ ⊆ (spt T)ᶜ, so by monotonicity and step 2, σ(Fᶜ) ≤ σ((spt T)ᶜ) = 0, i.e. σ(Fᶜ) = 0.
4. (⇐) Assume σ(Fᶜ) = 0 and let x ∈ spt T. Suppose, for contradiction, that x ∉ F. Since F is closed, Fᶜ is open, so there is ε > 0 with ball(x, ε) ⊆ Fᶜ (Metric.isOpen_iff); hence σ(ball(x, ε)) ≤ σ(Fᶜ) = 0. On the other hand dimred_im_mass_measure, part (b), applied with U = ℝ^P (open), R representing T and x ∈ ℝ^P, states that x ∈ spt T if and only if σ(ball(x, ε')) ≠ 0 for every ε' > 0; as x ∈ spt T, σ(ball(x, ε)) ≠ 0, a contradiction. Hence x ∈ F, and spt T ⊆ F. ∎
proof_key_steps: (spt T)ᶜ = zeroRegion T is open, hence Borel.
μHE[n](carrier ∖ spt T) = 0 (imrep_carrier_sdiff_support_null) gives (H^n⌞carrier)((spt T)ᶜ) = 0, so σ((spt T)ᶜ) = 0 by absolute continuity of withDensity.
(⇐) for x ∈ spt T ∖ F pick ball(x, ε) ⊆ Fᶜ; σ(ball) = 0 contradicts dimred_im_mass_measure (b).

subproblems.title: The support of a product current [[E]] × A lies in E + spt A
subproblems.statement: Let P, k, m', n' ∈ ℕ, E ⊆ ℝ^P compact, A ∈ 𝒟_{m'}(ℝ^P) with spt A compact and an integer multiplicity representation R_A of A (R_A.Represents A), and B ∈ 𝒟_{n'}(ℝ^P) with an integer multiplicity representation R_B (R_B.Represents B). Suppose R_B.measure(C) = ∫⁻_{t ∈ E} R_A.measure((y ↦ t + y)⁻¹(C)) dμHE[k](t) for every Borel set C. Then spt B ⊆ E + spt A = {t + y : t ∈ E, y ∈ spt A} (Set.image2 (fun t y => t + y) E A.support).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P k m' n' : ℕ) (E : Set (Euclid P)) (A : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) m') (RA : IMRep (univ : Set (Euclid P)) m') (B : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n') (RB : IMRep (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n'), IsCompact E → IsCompact A.support → RA.Represents A → RB.Represents B → (∀ C : Set (Euclid P), MeasurableSet C → RB.measure C = ∫⁻ t in E, RA.measure ((fun y => t + y) ⁻¹' C) ∂μHE[k]) → B.support ⊆ Set.image2 (fun t y => t + y) E A.support
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Step 6 of the parent proof (support of B = [[Q_r]] × Y), for a general compact E and current A.
Sibling used: support_measure (Submission.dimred_cs_sos_mt_cc_support_subset_iff_measure: for T ∈ 𝒟_j(ℝ^P) represented by R and closed F, spt T ⊆ F ↔ R.measure(Fᶜ) = 0).
Let F := {t + y : t ∈ E, y ∈ spt A} = Set.image2 (fun t y => t + y) E (spt A).

1. F is compact: it is the image of the compact set E × spt A under the continuous map (t, y) ↦ t + y (IsCompact.add, since image2 (+) E (spt A) is the pointwise sum E + spt A). Hence F is closed and Fᶜ is open, in particular Borel. Also E is compact, hence closed and Borel.
2. R_A.measure((spt A)ᶜ) = 0: spt A is compact, hence closed, and spt A ⊆ spt A; the sibling support_measure (direction ⇒), applied to A, R_A and the closed set spt A, gives R_A.measure((spt A)ᶜ) = 0.
3. For each t ∈ E, (y ↦ t + y)⁻¹(Fᶜ) ⊆ (spt A)ᶜ: if y ∈ spt A then t + y ∈ F by definition of F, so t + y ∉ Fᶜ. By monotonicity and step 2, R_A.measure((y ↦ t + y)⁻¹(Fᶜ)) = 0 for every t ∈ E.
4. Apply the hypothesis to the Borel set C := Fᶜ: R_B.measure(Fᶜ) = ∫⁻_{t ∈ E} R_A.measure((y ↦ t + y)⁻¹(Fᶜ)) dμHE[k](t) ≤ ∫⁻_{t ∈ E} 0 dμHE[k](t) = 0, where the inequality is monotonicity of the set lintegral over the measurable set E (setLIntegral_mono'), the integrand being 0 at every t ∈ E by step 3. Hence R_B.measure(Fᶜ) = 0.
5. The sibling support_measure (direction ⇐), applied to B, R_B and the closed set F, gives spt B ⊆ F. ∎
proof_key_steps: F := image2 (+) E (spt A) is compact (image of E × spt A under addition), hence closed with Borel complement.
For t ∈ E, (t + ·)⁻¹(Fᶜ) ⊆ (spt A)ᶜ, so the integrand of R_B.measure(Fᶜ) = ∫⁻_E R_A.measure((t + ·)⁻¹(Fᶜ)) vanishes on E and R_B.measure(Fᶜ) = 0.
support_measure (⇐) for B and the closed set F gives spt B ⊆ F.

subproblems.title: Geometry of the cube Q_r and of Q_r + K for K ⊆ G^⊥
subproblems.statement: Let P, k ∈ ℕ, g = (g_1, …, g_k) (g : Fin k → Euclid P) orthonormal with span G, r ∈ ℝ, q := G^⊥.starProjection, Q_r := {t ∈ G : |⟨g_i, t⟩| ≤ r for all i}, and let K ⊆ G^⊥ be compact. Then (i) Q_r is compact; (ii) Q_r + K = {t + y : t ∈ Q_r, y ∈ K} (Set.image2 (fun t y => t + y) Q_r K) is compact; and (iii) Q_r + K ⊆ {x : |⟨g_i, x⟩| ≤ r for all i} ∩ q⁻¹(K).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P k : ℕ) (g : Fin k → Euclid P) (r : ℝ) (K : Set (Euclid P)), Orthonormal ℝ g → IsCompact K → K ⊆ ((Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range g))ᗮ : Set (Euclid P)) → IsCompact {t | t ∈ Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range g) ∧ ∀ i, |inner ℝ (g i) t| ≤ r} ∧ IsCompact (Set.image2 (fun t y => t + y) {t | t ∈ Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range g) ∧ ∀ i, |inner ℝ (g i) t| ≤ r} K) ∧ Set.image2 (fun t y => t + y) {t | t ∈ Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range g) ∧ ∀ i, |inner ℝ (g i) t| ≤ r} K ⊆ {x | ∀ i, |inner ℝ (g i) x| ≤ r} ∩ (Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range g))ᗮ.starProjection ⁻¹' K
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Steps 3, 6 and 7 of the parent proof ("Q_r is closed (hence Borel)", "Q_r is closed and bounded, spt Y is compact", "F ⊆ {x : |⟨g_i, x⟩| ≤ r for all i} ∩ q⁻¹(spt Y): for x = t + y with t ∈ Q_r ⊆ G and y ∈ spt Y ⊆ G^⊥, ⟨g_i, x⟩ = ⟨g_i, t⟩ ... and q(x) = q(t) + q(y) = 0 + y"), with K in place of spt Y.

1. (Expansion in G.) Every t ∈ G satisfies t = Σ_i ⟨g_i, t⟩ g_i. Indeed, t ∈ span(range g) gives coefficients c : Fin k → ℝ with t = Σ_b c_b g_b (Submodule.mem_span_range_iff_exists_fun). For each i, ⟨g_i, t⟩ = Σ_b c_b ⟨g_i, g_b⟩ = c_i, because ⟨g_i, g_i⟩ = ‖g_i‖² = 1 and ⟨g_i, g_b⟩ = 0 for b ≠ i (orthonormality). Replacing each c_i by ⟨g_i, t⟩ gives the expansion.
2. (Q_r is closed.) G is a finite-dimensional subspace of ℝ^P, hence closed (Submodule.closed_of_finiteDimensional). For each i the map t ↦ |⟨g_i, t⟩| is continuous, so {t : |⟨g_i, t⟩| ≤ r} is closed, and so is the intersection over i. Q_r is the intersection of G with this set, hence closed.
3. (Q_r is bounded.) For t ∈ Q_r, step 1 and the triangle inequality give ‖t‖ = ‖Σ_i ⟨g_i, t⟩ g_i‖ ≤ Σ_i |⟨g_i, t⟩|·‖g_i‖ = Σ_i |⟨g_i, t⟩| ≤ k·r. Hence Q_r ⊆ closedBall(0, k·r), a bounded set (if r < 0, Q_r is empty and this holds trivially).
4. (Compactness, (i) and (ii).) ℝ^P is a proper metric space, so the closed bounded set Q_r is compact (Metric.isCompact_of_isClosed_isBounded). The set Q_r + K = image2 (+) Q_r K is the image of the compact set Q_r × K under the continuous addition map, hence compact (IsCompact.add).
5. (Inclusion (iii).) Let x = t + y with t ∈ Q_r and y ∈ K, so y ∈ G^⊥. For each i, g_i ∈ G (Submodule.subset_span), hence ⟨g_i, y⟩ = 0 (Submodule.inner_right_of_mem_orthogonal) and ⟨g_i, x⟩ = ⟨g_i, t⟩ + ⟨g_i, y⟩ = ⟨g_i, t⟩, so |⟨g_i, x⟩| = |⟨g_i, t⟩| ≤ r. Further, q is linear; t ∈ G ⊆ (G^⊥)^⊥ (Submodule.le_orthogonal_orthogonal), so q(t) = 0 (Submodule.starProjection_apply_eq_zero_iff), and y ∈ G^⊥ gives q(y) = y (Submodule.starProjection_eq_self_iff). Thus q(x) = q(t) + q(y) = y ∈ K, i.e. x ∈ q⁻¹(K). Hence x ∈ {x : |⟨g_i, x⟩| ≤ r for all i} ∩ q⁻¹(K). ∎
proof_key_steps: For t ∈ G = span(g), orthonormality gives t = Σ_i ⟨g_i, t⟩ g_i.
Q_r is closed (G closed as a finite-dimensional subspace; |⟨g_i, ·⟩| ≤ r closed) and bounded by ‖t‖ ≤ Σ_i |⟨g_i, t⟩| ≤ k r, hence compact; Q_r + K is compact as the image of Q_r × K under addition.
For x = t + y (t ∈ Q_r, y ∈ K ⊆ G^⊥): ⟨g_i, x⟩ = ⟨g_i, t⟩ so |⟨g_i, x⟩| ≤ r, and q(x) = q(t) + q(y) = 0 + y ∈ K.

subproblems.title: An integer multiplicity cycle from a boundary relation ∂B = T₂ + (−1)^p T₁
subproblems.statement: Let P, n, p ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P open, B ∈ 𝒟_{n+2}(U) (GeometricCurrentOn U (n+1+1)) and integer multiplicity T₁, T₂ ∈ 𝒟_{n+1}(U) such that ∂B(ω) = T₂(ω) + (−1)^p·T₁(ω) for every test (n+1)-form ω in U. Then there are Z, E' ∈ 𝒟_{n+1}(U) such that Z is integer multiplicity, ∂Z = 0 (BoundaryVanishes Z), spt Z ⊆ spt B, M(E') ≤ M(T₂), and Z(ω) = T₁(ω) + E'(ω) for every test (n+1)-form ω in U. (Z = (−1)^p ∂B, E' = (−1)^p T₂.)
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (B : GeometricCurrentOn U (n + 1 + 1)) (T₁ T₂ : GeometricCurrentOn U (n + 1)) (p : ℕ), IsOpen U → IsIntegerMultiplicity T₁ → IsIntegerMultiplicity T₂ → (∀ ω : TestFormOn U (n + 1), B.boundary ω = T₂ ω + (-1 : ℝ) ^ p * T₁ ω) → ∃ Z E' : GeometricCurrentOn U (n + 1), IsIntegerMultiplicity Z ∧ BoundaryVanishes Z ∧ Z.support ⊆ B.support ∧ E'.mass ≤ T₂.mass ∧ ∀ ω : TestFormOn U (n + 1), Z ω = T₁ ω + E' ω
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Step 5 and the first sentence of Step 7 of the parent proof (Z := B_X + c·E'', E' := c·E'', c = (−1)^k, Z = c·∂B, integer multiplicity by rsd_isIntegerMultiplicity_int_combination, ∂Z = 0 by ∂∂ = 0, M(E') ≤ M(E'') by mass_triangle, spt Z ⊆ spt B), with T₁ = B_X, T₂ = E'' and a general exponent p.
Sibling used: support_smul_boundary (Submission.dimred_cs_sos_mt_cc_support_smul_boundary: S(ω) = c·∂T(ω) for all ω ⇒ spt S ⊆ spt T). Accepted results cited by name (dependencies of ancestors of this node): rsd_isIntegerMultiplicity_int_combination (∀ P n U T₁ T₂ S (p₁ p₂ : ℤ), IsOpen U → IsIntegerMultiplicity T₁ → IsIntegerMultiplicity T₂ → (∀ ω, S ω = p₁·T₁ ω + p₂·T₂ ω) → IsIntegerMultiplicity S) and mass_triangle = lcmp_massOn_le_add_of_eval_eq (∀ P k U G (X Y Z : GeometricCurrentOn U k) (c : ℝ), |c| ≤ 1 → (∀ ω, tsupport ω ⊆ G → Z ω = X ω + c·Y ω) → Z.massOn G ≤ X.massOn G + Y.massOn G).
Let c := (−1)^p ∈ ℝ. Then c·c = ((−1)·(−1))^p = 1 and |c| = |−1|^p = 1.

1. (Definition.) Define Z, E' ∈ 𝒟_{n+1}(U) as the scalar multiples Z := c·∂B and E' := c·T₂, i.e. their underlying linear functionals are c • (∂B).toCurrent and c • T₂.toCurrent, so Z(ω) = c·∂B(ω) and E'(ω) = c·T₂(ω). They are continuous currents: if ω_j → 0 in the test-form topology of U then ∂B(ω_j) → 0 and T₂(ω_j) → 0 (continuity of the currents ∂B and T₂), hence c·∂B(ω_j) → 0 and c·T₂(ω_j) → 0.
2. (Action.) For every test (n+1)-form ω, by the hypothesis, Z(ω) = c·(T₂(ω) + c·T₁(ω)) = c·T₂(ω) + (c·c)·T₁(ω) = T₁(ω) + E'(ω).
3. (Integer multiplicity.) By step 2, Z(ω) = 1·T₁(ω) + c·T₂(ω) for every ω, where 1 and (−1)^p are integers whose real casts are 1 and c. Since U is open and T₁, T₂ are integer multiplicity, rsd_isIntegerMultiplicity_int_combination (with p₁ = 1, p₂ = (−1)^p ∈ ℤ, S = Z) shows that Z is integer multiplicity.
4. (∂Z = 0.) Since Z has degree n + 1, BoundaryVanishes Z means Z.boundary = 0. For a test n-form φ, using GeometricCurrentOn.boundary_apply twice, ∂Z(φ) = Z(dφ) = c·∂B(dφ) = c·(∂(∂B))(φ) = c·0 = 0, because ∂(∂B) = 0 (GeometricCurrentOn.boundary_boundary, a consequence of d∘d = 0, exteriorDerivative_sq). By extensionality of currents, Z.boundary = 0.
5. (Support.) Z(ω) = c·∂B(ω) for every ω, so the sibling support_smul_boundary, applied with T := B, S := Z and the constant c, gives spt Z ⊆ spt B.
6. (Mass.) Apply mass_triangle, i.e. lcmp_massOn_le_add_of_eval_eq, to the currents X := 0, Y := T₂, Z := E' in 𝒟_{n+1}(U), the constant c (|c| = 1 ≤ 1) and the region G := U: for every test form ω (in particular every ω with tsupport ω ⊆ U), E'(ω) = 0 + c·T₂(ω) = 0(ω) + c·T₂(ω). This yields M_U(E') ≤ M_U(0) + M_U(T₂). The local mass M_U(0) is the supremum of ofReal(0(ω)) = ofReal 0 = 0 over the admissible forms ω, hence equals 0. Since M(V) = M_U(V) for every V ∈ 𝒟_{n+1}(U) (GeometricCurrentOn.mass), M(E') ≤ M(T₂).
Steps 2–6 establish all the conclusions for Z and E'. ∎
proof_key_steps: Set c = (−1)^p (c² = 1, |c| = 1) and define the currents Z := c·∂B, E' := c·T₂.
Z(ω) = c·T₂(ω) + c²·T₁(ω) = T₁(ω) + E'(ω); hence Z = 1·T₁ + (−1)^p·T₂ is integer multiplicity (rsd_isIntegerMultiplicity_int_combination).
∂Z(φ) = c·∂∂B(φ) = 0; spt Z ⊆ spt B by support_smul_boundary.
M(E') ≤ M(0) + M(T₂) = M(T₂) by lcmp_massOn_le_add_of_eval_eq (mass_triangle) with X = 0, constant c, region U.
